2027-03-06.title: Fourth Saturday of the Great Fast
2027-03-06.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Never has anyone spoken like this
2027-03-06.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-03-06.verse: The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
theo: Paul writes to Christians living in the capital of the empire, under rulers who were not Christian and not always just: “Let every person be subject to the governing authorities; for there is no authority except from God, and those authorities that exist have been instituted by God.” He is not flattering the emperor. He is saying that ordered government, which protects the weak and restrains the violent, is part of God's providence, and that the ruler is meant to be “God's servant for your good.” So Christians pay their taxes honestly, give respect and honour where they are due, and obey “not only because of wrath but also because of conscience.” Elsewhere the Church learned the limit of this obedience from the apostles themselves: when the authorities forbade them to preach Christ, Peter answered, “We must obey God rather than any human authority” (Acts 5:29). Jesus had already drawn the line: “Give therefore to the emperor the things that are the emperor's, and to God the things that are God's” (Matthew 22:21). The St Thomas Christians lived this balance for centuries under Hindu kings. The Tharisappalli copper plates of 849 record the privileges granted to the Christian community of Quilon by a local ruler, and our forefathers were known as loyal subjects and honest traders. A Christian citizen today pays tax without cheating, does not bribe, votes with conscience, prays for those in authority, and refuses only what is against God.

In the Gospel the chief priests and Pharisees had sent temple police to arrest Jesus. The police come back empty-handed. “Why did you not arrest him?” Their answer is one of the simplest confessions in the Gospel: “Never has anyone spoken like this!” They were not theologians; they had only listened. Their superiors are angry: “Surely you have not been deceived too, have you? Has any one of the authorities or of the Pharisees believed in him?” Then one voice rises in the council. Nicodemus, “who had gone to Jesus before, and who was one of them”, asks a careful question: “Our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing to find out what they are doing, does it?” It is not yet a bold confession, only a plea for fairness, and he is mocked for it: “Surely you are not also from Galilee, are you?” But this small courage grows. On Good Friday the same Nicodemus will come openly to the Cross, “bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, weighing about a hundred pounds” (John 19:39), to bury the Lord. The Passion is drawing near. In families, parishes and offices, someone is always being condemned without a hearing. The Great Fast asks us for the courage of Nicodemus: to say, quietly and clearly, let us first hear him.
outline: Ask: am I an honest citizen and a fair judge?
Taxes, respect and conscience, and the limit: God first.
Point 2 · Never has anyone spoken like this
live: Check that your taxes, bills and documents are honest, and refuse any bribe this week, given or taken.
When someone is being criticised in their absence, say: let us first hear their side.
2027-03-06.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, the guards who came to arrest you went away saying: never has anyone spoken like this. Give us ears to listen to your word, honest hands in our duties as citizens, and the courage of Nicodemus to defend those who are condemned without a hearing. Bless all who govern, that they may serve the good of all, and keep us always faithful to God above every human power. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we hear the voice of which the guards said, never has anyone spoken like this, and we receive the One whom Nicodemus buried and the Father raised.

quick: Paul: authority comes from God and is meant to serve the good; pay taxes, give respect, obey with conscience.
The limit: we must obey God rather than any human authority.
The police said: never has anyone spoken like this; Nicodemus asked that Jesus be given a hearing.
2027-03-06.action: When someone is criticised in their absence, ask that they first be heard.
2027-03-06.question: Do I condemn people without giving them a hearing?

family.explain: The leaders sent guards to arrest Jesus, but the guards came back without him. They said: no one has ever spoken like this man! Then a leader named Nicodemus said: we should listen to someone before we judge him. That was brave, because the others laughed at him. Later Nicodemus became a friend of Jesus in front of everyone.
family.intention: We pray for our country and for all who govern, that they may be honest and just.
family.ask: Ask: “When did we hear someone being blamed without being heard? What could we say next time?”

illus: In a staff room in a school near Changanassery, the teachers were agreeing that a new colleague had taken money from the class fund. One older teacher, who said very little at staff meetings, put down her tea and said: “Has anyone asked her?” There was an awkward silence. The next day it turned out that the money had been taken to pay a sick student's hospital bill, with the principal's permission. The new teacher never forgot the one colleague who had asked for a hearing.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, never has anyone spoken like you. Open our ears to your word. Amen.
share: Let every person be subject to the governing authorities (Romans 13:1). Am I honest in my duties as a citizen?
Never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:46). When did the word of Jesus last stop me in my tracks?
Our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing (John 7:51). Whom have I judged without hearing?
pm.resp: Lord, give us ears to hear you.
interc: For the Church, that she may always obey God first.
For all who govern, in our country and our state, that they may serve the common good.
For those condemned without a fair hearing.
For all who seek Jesus by night, like Nicodemus, that they may find the courage to follow him openly.
For our group, that we may be honest citizens and fair judges.
pm.close: Father, all authority comes from you. Make us faithful citizens, fair in judgement and honest in our duties, and above all faithful to your Son, whose word is like no other. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes: let every person be subject to the governing authorities; for there is no authority except from God (Romans 13:1). Authority is meant to be God's servant for our good. So a Christian pays tax honestly, refuses bribes, gives respect and prays for those who govern.

But there is a limit. When the authorities forbade the apostles to preach, Peter said: we must obey God rather than any human authority (Acts 5:29). We give to the emperor what is his, and to God what is God's.

The guards sent to arrest Jesus came back empty-handed and said: never has anyone spoken like this! (John 7:46). They had only listened. If we listen to Jesus with open hearts during this fast, his word will stop us too.

Nicodemus asked the council: does our law judge people without first giving them a hearing? (John 7:51). It was a small act of courage, and it grew until he came openly to bury the Lord. Let us also defend those who are judged without a hearing. Amen.
kids: Children, the guards went to catch Jesus, but when they heard him speak they came back and said: no one ever talked like this man! Let us listen to Jesus too. And when someone is being blamed, let us say: let's hear their side first!

intro: Theme: “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
The Christian as citizen under God, the guards who only listened, and Nicodemus who asked for a fair hearing.

q: By me kings reign, and rulers decree what is just;
Let every person be subject to the governing authorities; for there is no authority except from God, and those authorities that exist have been instituted by God.
points.apply: Make sure your taxes, bills and documents are honest, and refuse every bribe.

points.h: Never has anyone spoken like this
q: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their own people; I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.
The police answered, “Never has anyone spoken like this!”
points.apply: Read the Passion according to John slowly before Palm Sunday, as if hearing it for the first time.

q: You must not be partial in judging: hear out the small and the great alike; you shall not be intimidated by anyone, for the judgment is God's. Any case that is too hard for you, bring to me, and I will hear it.”
“Our law does not judge people without first giving them a hearing to find out what they are doing, does it?”
points.apply: When someone is criticised in their absence, ask that their side be heard first.

concl: A Christian is an honest citizen, a careful listener and a fair judge, faithful to God above all.
Listen to the One whose word is like no other, and find the courage of Nicodemus.
2027-03-06.resolve: This week, be honest in every duty, and defend one person who is being judged without a hearing.
